That's because the regex `(.+?) *` is non-greedy - it matches as few characters as possible while still allowing the rest of the pattern to match. Since ` *` can match 0 spaces, `.+?` only needs to match one character.

But parse() works differently - it uses `^` and `$` anchors (fullmatch), so `(.+?) *` must consume the entire string. In that case, `.+?` expands to match "hello world" since there's nothing after it.
